title: Space Invaders
description: Build a complete Space Invaders game in Scratch 3. This self-guided advanced-beginner course is for ages 10-14 with about one year of Scratch experience. You will create an alien fleet that moves together, two reusable shots, bunkers that show damage, a bonus Mothership, scoring, and clear ways to win and lose.
objectives: Use coordinates, loops, conditions, variables, messages, and clones in Scratch 3.
Create 24 Alien clones in an 8 by 3 grid and move them as one fleet.
Control game phases and messages with scripts on the Stage.
Build reusable Player Laser and Enemy Shot sprites without cloning either shot.
Give Bunker clones independent health and costume damage.
Finish a game with scoring, a bonus Mothership, and reliable win and loss rules.
prerequisites: You have used Scratch for about one year and can create a blank Scratch 3 project.
You can connect scripts, choose values from block menus, rename sprites, and use basic loops and conditions.
You do not need to have built a full game or used clones before.
requirements: Use Scratch 3 in a modern web browser or the Scratch desktop app.
Complete all six chapters in order; this course has one required path.
Plan for 90-120 minutes per chapter. At each chapter checkpoint, use File > Save to your computer. To continue later, open Scratch and use File > Load from your computer.
Use the exact sprite, variable, costume, backdrop, and message names shown so the code references match.
Keep every costume centered and inside the maximum width and height given in Chapter 1 so separate targets cannot overlap.
Use the green flag as the only way to start or restart the game.

vocabulary.meaning: A number that describes a sprite position. X moves left and right; Y moves down and up.
A temporary copy of a sprite that runs the clone scripts and keeps its own sprite-only variable values.
A shared variable made with `For all sprites`. The Stage and every sprite can read or change it.
A variable made with `For this sprite only`. Each clone gets its own value for that variable.
A named broadcast that starts matching `when I receive` scripts.
A stored value such as `starting`, `playing`, `won`, or `lost` that describes what the game may do now.
One sprite that is hidden, moved, and used again instead of creating clones.
A 0-or-1 variable that shows whether a reusable sprite is busy. Checking it prevents the same action from happening twice.
One vertical firing column in the eight-column alien fleet.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Build the Launch Pad
objectives: Plan the game objects and rules before coding.
Create all named sprites, variables, messages, and backdrops.
Make one green-flag reset sequence on the Stage.
Move the Player while keeping it on the Stage.

steps.title: Map the Complete Game
steps.explanation: A reliable game starts with a clear plan. The Stage will reset shared data and control the alien march. One Alien sprite will make 24 clones. Player Laser, Enemy Shot, and Mothership will each be one reusable sprite with no clones. Each of the three Bunker clones will remember its own Health value.
instructions: Open a new Scratch 3 project and delete the Cat sprite.
Write down the required sprites: `Player`, `Alien`, `Player Laser`, `Enemy Shot`, `Bunker`, and `Mothership`.
Picture an 8-column by 3-row alien fleet. That is 24 aliens, so `Aliens Left` starts at 24 and the player wins when it reaches 0.
Trace the two ways to lose: an Enemy Shot touches Player, or an Alien reaches the invasion line.
Remember the restart rule: after a win or loss, click the green flag. Do not build a Restart button or an in-game restart message.
hints: One reusable sprite works well when only one laser or shot of that type may be active.
One message tells every Alien clone to update for the same fleet step.

debuggingTips.symptom: The plan includes many laser or shot clones.
checks: Cross out plans to clone either shot. `Player Laser` and `Enemy Shot` will hide, move, and be reused.
Keep clones only for `Alien` and `Bunker`.

checkpoint.task: Explain the object plan without looking back at the lesson.
checkpoint.expectedResult: You can name all six sprites, the two sprite types that use clones, the two reusable shots that do not use clones, and both ways to lose.
completeWhen: You identify `Alien` and `Bunker` as the only cloned sprites.
You identify the green flag as the only restart.
You explain that `Aliens Left` reaching zero causes the win.

steps.title: Create the Stage and Six Sprites
steps.explanation: Names matter because Scratch places sprite names inside sensing and motion blocks. Set up every game object now so later instructions can use exact names.
instructions: Create the `Space` backdrop. Paint and rename the existing blank backdrop, or choose a dark space backdrop, delete the original blank backdrop, and rename the chosen one `Space`.
Write the controls on `Space`: Arrow keys move, Space fires, and the green flag starts or restarts.
Write the goal and scoring on `Space`: destroy all Aliens to win, avoid Enemy Shots, stop the Aliens from reaching the invasion line, Aliens score 10, and Mothership scores 50.
Draw a thin, faint line across `Space` at y -60 and label it as the invasion line. An alien that drops below this line ends the game.
Duplicate Space twice. Name the copies `You Win` and `Game Over`, replace the control text with a large matching result, and confirm exactly three backdrops exist.
Create a ship sprite named `Player`. Center its artwork and keep its visible costume no larger than 36 pixels wide by 18 pixels high.
Create an enemy sprite named `Alien`. Center its artwork and keep its visible costume no larger than 32 pixels wide by 18 pixels high.
Paint centered vertical sprites named `Player Laser` and `Enemy Shot`. Keep each visible costume no larger than 4 pixels wide by 10 pixels high; make Player Laser bright and Enemy Shot red.
Create a centered `Bunker` no larger than 56 pixels wide by 18 pixels high and a centered `Mothership` no larger than 40 pixels wide by 12 pixels high.
Check costume selection bounds in the paint editor. Do not continue with off-center pixels or artwork outside the stated maximum boxes.
hints: Simple geometric art is easier to resize and test than detailed art.
Select the Stage before editing backdrop names.

checks: Check spelling and spaces in every sprite name.
Make sure `Player Laser` and `Enemy Shot` are two different sprites.

steps.title: Create Variables and Messages
steps.explanation: The Stage and sprites need the same names for game information. Variables made `For all sprites` store shared facts and fleet coordinates. Variables made `For this sprite only` let each Alien clone remember its own row and column and each Bunker clone remember its own health.
instructions: Make these variables with `For all sprites`: `Score`, `Aliens Left`, `Game State`, `Stage`, `Fleet X`, `Fleet Y`, `Laser Active`, `Enemy Shot Active`, and `Shot Lane`.
On the Alien sprite, make `My Column`, `My Row`, and `Is Clone` with `For this sprite only`.
On the Bunker sprite, make `Health` and `Bunker Number` with `For this sprite only`.
On the Mothership sprite, make `Active` with `For this sprite only`.
On the Stage, drag out a temporary `broadcast` block. Open its message menu, choose New message, and create `Reset Game` and `Start Game`.
Later chapters create each new message when its first real script is built. This keeps unused message blocks out of this checkpoint.
Keep the temporary broadcast block until you build the startup script on the Stage in the next step and select `Reset Game` and `Start Game` in its broadcast blocks.
After both messages are used in the startup script, delete the temporary broadcast block.
Hide every variable monitor except `Score` and `Aliens Left`.
hints: The choice `For this sprite only` appears while making a variable.
Capitalization must match because the finished code uses these exact names.

checks: Delete and remake `Health` as `For this sprite only` on Bunker.

steps.title: Reset the Game and Control Player
steps.explanation: One script on the Stage is the only way the game starts. It resets shared values, tells every sprite to prepare, and starts play only after preparation finishes. Player checks the arrow keys in its own movement loop and keeps its x coordinate inside the Stage. A later chapter adds a separate firing loop, so waiting for the Space key to be released never pauses movement.
instructions: On the Stage, add the green-flag script shown below. Use `broadcast Reset Game and wait` so all setup finishes before `Game State` becomes `playing`.
On Player, reset its position to x 0, y -150 and show it when `Reset Game` arrives.
On Alien, Player Laser, Enemy Shot, Bunker, and Mothership, add a `when I receive Reset Game` script with `hide`.
This hides every non-Player sprite during Chapter 1 setup and every reset. In later chapters, add each sprite's other reset blocks to this same script.
On Player, start a movement script when `Start Game` arrives. Add `repeat until`, and for its condition put `Game State = playing` inside a `not` block. Movement then stops when the game ends.
Move left or right by 6 while the matching arrow key is pressed.
Keep Player between x -210 and x 210 so it cannot leave the Stage.
Click the green flag and test both edges.
hints: Put the two edge checks inside the movement loop, after the movement blocks.
The Stage uses `broadcast Reset Game and wait`, so it does not send `Start Game` until every `when I receive Reset Game` script has finished.

debuggingTips.symptom: Player moves once and stops.
checks: Put all key and edge checks inside the `repeat until Game State is not playing` loop.
Use sensing blocks `key left arrow pressed?` and `key right arrow pressed?`.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Control the Alien Fleet
objectives: Build exactly 24 Alien clones in an 8 by 3 grid.
Store each clone's row and column in `For this sprite only` variables.

steps.title: Make Alien Clones from the Hidden Original
steps.explanation: The hidden original Alien creates all the clones. Before it creates each clone, it changes its own row and column values. Scratch copies those `For this sprite only` values into the new clone, so every Alien clone remembers its row and column.
instructions: Select Alien and confirm `My Column`, `My Row`, and `Is Clone` say `For this sprite only`.
Confirm the centered Alien costume is no larger than 32 pixels wide by 18 pixels high so rows and columns cannot overlap.
Find Alien's existing `when I receive Reset Game` script from Chapter 1. Under its `hide` block, add the cloning blocks shown below. Do not add a second `when I receive Reset Game` event block.
Set `Is Clone` to 1 before creating clones and back to 0 afterward. This tells the hidden original apart from its clones.
Change `Aliens Left` by 1 for each clone so the final count is exactly 24.
hints: The inner loop makes eight columns; the outer loop makes three rows.
A clone receives copies of the original's `For this sprite only` values when `create clone of myself` runs.

steps.explanation: Only the Stage changes `Fleet X` and `Fleet Y`. It then broadcasts one of three march messages. Each live clone uses the same formula to work out its new position. This keeps the rows and columns evenly spaced after other clones are destroyed.

After `go to x y`, add an `if` that checks `y position < -60` and `Game State = playing`.
Inside that `if`, set Game State to lost. Then choose New message in the broadcast block, create `Lose`, and broadcast it.

Keep the `Is Clone = 1` check so the hidden original does not act like a fleet member.

steps.title: Control the Fleet in Three Movement Phases
steps.explanation: The Stage controls the fleet with scripts that finish each phase instead of letting 24 clones choose their own movement. In phase 1, the fleet moves right five times. In phase 2, it moves left nine times. In phase 3, it moves right nine times. Each side-to-side phase ends with one move down. The `Stage` variable then switches between 2 and 3.
instructions: On the Stage, start a new script with `when I receive Start Game`. The steps below build the march script shown at the end.
Add `repeat until`. For its condition, put `Game State = playing` inside a `not` block.

Inside the repeat, add an `if then else` that checks `Stage = 1`. Inside its `else`, add a second `if then else` that checks `Stage = 2`. The three open spaces will hold phase 1, phase 2, and phase 3.
In the `Stage = 1` space, build phase 1. Repeat five times: add 10 to `Fleet X`, use `broadcast March Right and wait`, and then wait 0.35 seconds.
After phase 1, subtract 10 from `Fleet Y`, use `broadcast March Down and wait`, and set the `Stage` variable to 2.
In the `Stage = 2` space, build phase 2 with nine left moves and one down move. Then set the `Stage` variable to 3.
In the last `else` space, build phase 3 with nine right moves and one down move. Then set the `Stage` variable to 2.
Wrap the blocks of every sideways move in `if Game State = playing`. Wrap every down move the same way. This makes the fleet stop as soon as the game ends.
Keep every coordinate change and march broadcast on the Stage.
hints: `Broadcast and wait` lets all clones finish positioning before the next fleet step.
The fleet starts in the center. Phase 1 moves it five steps to the right edge. The nine-step phases then travel the full width from edge to edge.
